title: Strict etale coefficient systems: clopen product and compact-support comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, without assuming $Y$ separated over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $I$ be finite and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions covering $X$, with $g_i=g\circ j_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Empty components and the empty cover of $X=\varnothing$ are allowed.

Choose a compactification $c=(a,p)$ and put $c_i=(a\circ j_i,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For a scheme $T$ let $\mathsf S_A(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ be the abelian category of strict systems $M_n$ of constant-$A_n$ module sheaves with $A_{n+1}$-linear transition maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$, and compatible families as morphisms. Use its ordinary unbounded derived category and its exact level evaluations $e_n$ [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Write $a_{!,A}$ for termwise open extension and $p_{A,*}$ for termwise direct image, with total derived direct image $Rp_{A,*}$ [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint].

Restriction induces an exact equivalence
$$\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}})\simeq\prod_{i\in I}\mathsf S_A((X_i)_{\mathrm{et}}).$$
Its inverse is finite product of zero insertions, with all coefficient actions and semilinear transitions componentwise. The equivalence induces an equivalence of unbounded derived categories, whose restriction $r_{i,A}$ and zero insertion $E_{i,A}$ are adjoint in both orders, with the units and counits induced termwise. Evaluation commutes with these functors and their adjunction maps. The empty product is the zero category.

On these actual derived system categories put $F_{g,A}=Rp_{A,*}a_{!,A}$ and $F_{g_i,A}=Rp_{A,*}(a\circ j_i)_{!,A}$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$b_{i,A}:F_{g,A}E_{i,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g_i,A}.$$
It is the image under $Rp_{A,*}$ of the exact open-extension compositor $a_{!,A}E_{i,A}\cong(a\circ j_i)_{!,A}$, normalized by the ordinary open-adjunction units. That compositor is an isomorphism of strict systems before localization, identity on each section over the component and zero off it, and commutes with all quotient transitions. Its finite evaluations are the ordinary etale finite-level open-extension and compact-support comparisons. This includes the action on morphisms, rather than independently selected maps after evaluation.

proof.text: First identify the given cover with a finite coproduct: morphisms from $X$ are exactly families of morphisms from the disjoint open subschemes $X_i$, since the component maps glue and there are no overlap conditions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product]. Its abelian-sheaf equivalence extends to constant-$A_n$ modules as follows: for each $a\in A_n$ transport the endomorphism $a\cdot(-)$ componentwise. Full faithfulness recovers these endomorphisms and their addition, multiplication and unit equations uniquely; it also recovers linear morphisms. The inverse on modules is $U\mapsto\prod_i M_i(U\times_X X_i)$. Indeed this is the sheaf reconstructed from its restrictions, and the module operations are componentwise. The construction commutes with restriction of scalars: both sides keep these same abelian sheaves and replace the action of $a$ by that of its image in the quotient ring.

source.place: Tag 0A5B, lemma-constant-smooth-statements, first proof paragraph; explicit module refinement of the cited clopen equivalence

proof.text: Apply step 1 at every $n$. A semilinear transition is a morphism $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$; step 1 identifies its source, target and Hom set componentwise, so it recovers precisely the family of component transitions. The equations for a compatible family of morphisms are recovered by faithfulness. Thus restriction $R$ and reconstruction $S$ are inverse functors on the actual strict systems of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Their inverse identifications commute with transitions, because each is the same section-restriction identification at every level. Exactness follows levelwise: at each level this is an additive equivalence of abelian categories, hence preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties. Evaluation commutes with all these constructions by their formulas.

source.place: Tag 0A5B, first proof paragraph; strict-system refinement written here

proof.text: In the product category let $Z_i$ insert an object in coordinate $i$ and zeros elsewhere. For a family $N$ and an object $M$ in component $i$, a map $Z_iM\to N$ is exactly its $i$th coordinate $M\to N_i$, while a map $N\to Z_iM$ is exactly $N_i\to M$: all other coordinates are the unique maps from or to zero. These inverse Hom correspondences are natural, giving $Z_i\dashv\mathrm{pr}_i\dashv Z_i$. Their units and counits are the coordinate identities together with zero-coordinate maps; the triangle identities hold coordinatewise. Transport through $R,S$ gives $E_{i,A}\dashv r_{i,A}\dashv E_{i,A}$ for strict systems. Also $S((M_i)_i)=\prod_i E_{i,A}M_i$: its restriction to coordinate $j$ is $M_j$ and the other factors are zero. These formulas commute with evaluation. If $I$ is empty the sheaf condition for the empty covering of the empty scheme forces every level to be zero; the system category is the zero category.

source.place: Tag 0A5B, disjoint-union reduction; elementary product-category calculation

proof.text: The functors $r_{i,A},E_{i,A},R,S$ are exact; finite assembly is exact because its kernels and cokernels are computed coordinatewise. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] apply each functor termwise to unbounded complexes and localize. The natural inverse maps of $R,S$ and all adjunction maps descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]; composition and identities are preserved, hence so are the inverse and triangle identities. More explicitly the functors $D(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))\to\prod_iD(\mathsf S_A((X_i)_{\mathrm{et}}))$ and $(K_i)_i\mapsto\bigoplus_i E_{i,A}K_i$ are inverse: coordinatewise $r_jE_i$ is the identity for $j=i$ and zero otherwise, and $\bigoplus_i E_ir_i\cong\mathrm{id}$ is the descended finite reconstruction map. Finite sums here equal finite products; their inclusions, projections and biproduct identities descend from complexes. The two adjunctions descend with their termwise units and counits. Evaluation is exact by [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]; its commutation with these functors and maps descends by the same localization property.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; localization of the finite reconstruction and adjunction identities

proof.text: Identify ordinary clopen extension $(j_i)_!$ with zero insertion: by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] it is left adjoint to restriction, as is zero insertion by step 3. The unique unit-compatible isomorphism of these two left adjoints is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. For $a$ and $j_i$, the restriction models compose as equal functors: on an etale object $V\to X_i$ both evaluate a sheaf at $V\to X_i\to X\to\overline X$. The composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the same uniqueness node therefore give $c_{i,n}:a_!(j_i)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(a j_i)_!$, with normalization $r_i r_a(c_{i,n})\circ r_i(\eta_a)\circ\eta_{j_i}=\eta_{a j_i}$. This is the canonical compositor of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. All these functors are exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied to the localized small etale sites and the constant coefficient ring.

The preceding ordinary maps commute with coefficient transitions before localization. To check this for a possibly nonflat quotient $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, regard the target as an $A_{n+1}$-module by restriction of scalars. The presheaf formula [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] inserts a section $s$ into the summand indexed by its factorization through the open. Applying a semilinear transition $t$ replaces this generator by $t(s)$ in the same summand, on both sides of the compositor; any zero summand maps to zero. The formula commutes with restriction to every etale test object. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the resulting equalities extend uniquely to the sheafifications (and to either iterated sheafification). By the explicit adjunction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], these section maps are exactly the unit-normalized maps in step 5. The inverse compositor has the inverse section formula and satisfies the same equalities. The unit-compatible zero-insertion identification also has identity on its component and zero on the complement, so satisfies the same transition check. Consequently $c_{i,A}:a_{!,A}E_{i,A}\cong(a j_i)_{!,A}$ is a natural isomorphism of strict systems. Naturality for a system morphism is the same calculation with $t(s)$ replaced by its image under that morphism.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, explicit presheaf and sheafification construction; semilinear generator check

proof.text: Open extension on systems is exact because exactness is levelwise [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison] and each level extension is exact [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Descend $c_{i,A}$ and its inverse using [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. For the common proper part $p$, apply the actual total derived functor $Rp_{A,*}$ of [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]. This gives $b_{i,A}:Rp_{A,*}a_{!,A}E_{i,A}\cong Rp_{A,*}(a j_i)_{!,A}$, with inverse $Rp_{A,*}(c_{i,A}^{-1})$. Naturality holds on all derived morphisms because this is the image of a natural isomorphism under a functor. Evaluation gives the ordinary finite-level compositor followed by $Rp_*$: the open comparison evaluates by step 6, and $e_nRp_{A,*}\cong Rp_*e_n$ is the natural comparison of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Its naturality identifies the evaluated action on every morphism. Empty components give only the unique zero maps throughout. No step uses separatedness of $Y$ over $k$.
